chapter: Second lining and the brass bands
title: How he was called to a funeral parade and what it was like
summary: White describes being sent for through neighbours, riding the car to the hall and marching out with the band to the cemetery and back.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well, y'all, y'all, y'all, you ain't got cigarettes? I say, no, I ain't got no cigarettes. Well, y'all, y'all, y'all, go best. Go get your pack of cigarettes. Well, now when they go play, now I might not see them before, I might not see them before next week or two weeks after. But they all, they all know me, you see. Now if they don't see me, they ask her, or they ask her little boy. Or say, uh, oh, Dorothy? Oh, Miss Horace? Says, uh, do you see, do you see Horace? She said, yes. I see, yeah, no. She said, yeah, I see Mr. Horace. Mr. Horace must be at the ballroom or at the corner somewhere. Well, you, will you do something for me? She said, yes. Tell Mr. Horace I want him to be at the hall for one o'clock. We got a, we got a funeral, we got a parade. Now when I come home, I might come home, about half past two, three o'clock, or four o'clock. Now if she don't, she don't tell me, she tell her little sister to tell me. She said, Horace? I said, what? They want you for one o'clock. I said, for where? At, at the Percy Burns Hall, or at the Economy Hall, or at the St. Dominic Hall. I said, okay. Now what I do, now I get my bar, I said, Dorothy? She said, what? I said, give me, number seven cents. Alright, she said, alright, let me go look into my pocketbook and get seven cents. Now she get her cents, she give me seven cents. I catch the, I catch the bus. I used to catch a car. I catch a car and going up there. I go to the St. Leatherman Hall. See all y'all standing up outside now. I walked up in there. The other policeman, detail for the parade, you understand? Now when I walked up in there, oh, hello Horace. I said, how y'all do? I said, oh, I just said, okay. I said, where y'all going? I said, we're going to Walkerstown. I said, you going to Walkerstown? I said, who that is? Such and such a one. I said, okay. I said, let's go. I'm ready for you now. They hate it now. Boom, boom, boom. If you don't play that. They rhyme. Then they rhyme. You see, they play that. We going on up. Then we play, we play sing-on. Until we hit a block. When they hit a block, we won't, we won't, we hit it when the little drum stops.

Boom, boom, boom. You see what they tell you? Six fourth time. Or eight fourth time. Well, you know what I mean? You turn your, you turn your cards over. Now you turn your cards, what's on it, you got it. And you, we gone then. Now we hit, when we hit up there, you had a policeman, policeman standing, policeman horse standing right there. I'm right, I'm right by, I'm right with you. Then he said, Peg, he says, where you going? I said, you want to ride? I said, I'm going to ride where? I said, you want to go to jail? I said, I ain't worried about going to that place. I said, I ain't worried. I said, why? I said, for what? I said, for the police, I said, for what you want to ride him for? You see? That's when you all ask him, what you want to ride him for? Well, we don't want no second hand. I want him there. He's minding my instrument. We ain't paying you for, we ain't paying you for arrest this man. We paying you to keep you, keep us out of trouble. Well, I'm coming on up with you all then, you see? I'm going with you all. Don't care where you all hit, I'm right there. Go to protection levee, go all over with you. Then come on back, come to the hall. We break up by the hall. We come in the hall. We come in the hall about six o'clock. But, yeah, but half past six, we come in the hall. Now, when we come in the hall, we break up in the hall. Now, you go to your, you know, you're going home and I come on here and watch myself. Going out in the street and go out if I got somewhere to go. I said, well, I said, well, I said, I'm not coming in tonight. I said, I tell you, I tell your mother, I'm not coming in tonight. I might come in tomorrow morning. Well, I might be out having fun, stay out all night, might stay until about twelve, one o'clock. Then I knock on the door. Who that? I said, that's me. She opened the door, come on inside. See my bride and go to bed. Now, I'm gone now. Then I stayed here for a long time. Then, out again, I'm gone. Now, I might go, might, sometime I go by the bay house. A little drummer used to be over the river. Play the bass drum.
